overview: The committee reviewed municipal climate and energy initiatives, including heat pump coaching, building decarbonization planning, and flood mitigation. Members also discussed tree planting efforts, public housing sustainability, pollinator gardens, and climate impact projections.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes from the May meeting.

items.title: Administrative Updates and Summer Meeting Planning
items.summary: Staff announced incoming summer interns, and members coordinated tabling for Electrify Medford at Circle the Square and planned an informal summer potluck meeting.

items.title: City Climate Initiatives Update
items.summary: Pike reported on Electrify Medford coach trainings, composting enrollment, the Hegner Center resilience hub grant, school HVAC contracts, and technical assistance from DOER for a municipal building decarbonization roadmap.

items.title: Stormwater Flooding and Infrastructure
items.summary: Members and staff discussed municipal emergency planning, sea level rise at the Amelia Earhart Dam, drainage upgrades planned for Bowen and Golden avenues, and sewer system separation.

items.title: Housing Authority Sustainability
items.summary: In response to resident questions about renewable energy in public housing, members discussed planned solar installations at Walkling Court and decarbonization planning across housing properties.

items.title: City Park Pollinator Gardens
items.summary: Ondras detailed an ongoing initiative to propose native pollinator meadows at five Medford public park locations in coordination with Tufts students and the Mystic River Watershed Association.

items.title: Community Tree Updates
items.summary: Members discussed CPA grant funding awarded to Trees Medford for a park tree inventory and an upcoming DCR listening session on tree replacements at McDonald Park.

items.title: Climate Impact Risk Maps
items.summary: The chair shared ProPublica national climate maps and county-level risk scorecards, leading to a discussion on regional economic impacts, air quality, and localized environmental justice factors.

items.title: Proposed Healthy Soils Presentation
items.summary: The committee supported a proposal to invite soil remediation expert Dr. Ralph Baker to speak on soil degradation, brownfields, and regenerative practices at the September meeting.
